title: कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशीय नेपाली भाषाको मानकीकरणको कार्यदिशा (Karnali and Sudurpaschim Regional Nepali Language Standardization Work Direction)
nepali: प्रस्तुत अध्ययन कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशमा बोलिने नेपाली भाषाको मानकीकरणको कार्यदिशा निर्माण गर्नमा केन्द्रित छ । कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशीय नेपालीका भेदलाई मानकीकरण गरी भाषिक एकता कायम गराउने कार्यदिशा निर्माण गर्ने उद्देश्य र ‘यी प्रदेशका नेपाली भाषाको मानकीकरण के कसरी सम्भव छ त ढाँचाको लेख बन्न गएको छ । यी प्रदेशमा बोलिने भाषिका समूहलाई पश्चिमी भाषिका समूह, केन्द्रीय भाषिका समूह र भेरी क्षेत्रीय भाषिका समूह गरी मुख्य तीन भाषिका समूहमा विभाजन गरेर अध्ययन गरिएको प्रस्तुत पङ्तिकारको पूर्वाध्ययन र यस क्षेत्रलाई आधार बनाएर गरिएका पूर्वाध्ययनहरूलाई आधार मानी यिनको मानकीकरणका उपायहरू सुझाउने काम गरिएको छ । प्रायोगिक भाषाविज्ञानअन्तर्गतको भाषायोजनाभित्र पर्ने मानकीकरणको सिद्धान्तलाई यस लेखमा सैद्धान्तिक पर्याधार बनाइएको छ । प्रत्येक भाषाको मानकीकरण गर्न उक्त भाषाको अत्यधिक प्रयोगमा जोड दिनुपर्छ। भाषाको जति धेरै प्रयोग हुन्छ त्यति नै त्यसले जीवन्त अवस्था प्राप्त गर्छ । भाषाको प्रयोग शिक्षा, सञ्चार, साहित्य, प्रशासन, कानुन, उद्योग आदि विविध क्षेत्रमा हुन्छ । यसका लागि कोश र व्याकरण निर्माणसँगै पत्रिकाहरूको प्रकाशन हुनुपर्छ । भाषिक भेद भिन्न भए भाषा नै भिन्न हुन्छ अन्यथा सोही भाषाको क्षेत्रीय भेद हुन्छ तर नेपालका सन्दर्भमा पुर्बेली पनि भाषिका नै हो तर त्यसले मानकस्वरूप प्राप्त गरेको छ । जबकि नेपाली भाषाको उत्पत्ति कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशमै भएको हो । भाषाको उत्पत्ति भएकै ठाउँमा बोलिने भाषाचाहिँ भाषिका तर सुदूरपूर्वमा बोलिने नेपालीचाहिँ भाषा भएको अवस्था छ । कर्णाली र सुदूर पश्चिम प्रदेशमा बोलिने नेपाली मानक नहुनाको प्रमुख कारण प्रयोगकै अभाव हो, नेपाली भाषाको प्रयोग गर्दाकै अवस्थामा यसको प्रयोगमा जोड दिएमा यस क्षेत्रको भाषालाई मानकीकरण गर्न सकिन्छ भन्ने सार यस लेखमा निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: The present study focuses on drawing up a work direction for the standardization of the Nepali language spoken in Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces. This article has been written with the aim of building a work direction that standardizes the differences within the Nepali of Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces and thereby secures linguistic unity, and it is framed around the question of how, then, the standardization of the Nepali language of these provinces is possible. The dialect groups spoken in these provinces were divided into three main dialect groups — the western dialect group, the central dialect group and the Bheri regional dialect group — and, using the present author's prior study, carried out by studying them in that way, and the prior studies carried out with this area as their base, the task of recommending measures for standardizing them has been done. The principle of standardization, which falls within language planning under applied linguistics, has been made the theoretical foundation in this article. To standardize each language, emphasis has to be put on heavy use of that language. The more a language is used, the more it attains a living condition. A language is used in various fields such as education, communication, literature, administration, law and industry. For this, dictionaries and grammars have to be produced, and periodicals have to be published alongside them. If the linguistic differences are distinct, the language itself is distinct; otherwise it is a regional variety of the same language, but in Nepal's context the eastern one is also a dialect, yet it has attained the status of the standard. And yet the Nepali language originated right in Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces. The situation is that the language spoken in the very place where the language originated is a dialect, while the Nepali spoken in the far east is a language. The main cause of the Nepali spoken in Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces not being standard is the lack of use itself; the gist drawn out in this article is that if emphasis is placed on its use in the very course of using the Nepali language, the language of this region can be standardized.
british_english: The present study is centred on establishing a course of action for the standardization of the Nepali language spoken in the Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces. The article has come to be written with the aim of devising a course of action that standardizes the variations of provincial Nepali in Karnali and Sudurpaschim and so maintains linguistic unity, and around the framework of the question of how standardization of the Nepali language of these provinces is at all possible. The dialect groups spoken in these provinces having been divided into three principal dialect groups — the western dialect group, the central dialect group and the Bheri regional dialect group — the present author's preliminary study, carried out by studying them upon that division, together with the preliminary studies undertaken with this region as their ground, have been taken as the basis, and the task of proposing measures for standardizing them has been carried out. The principle of standardization, which falls under language planning within applied linguistics, has been made the theoretical underpinning of this article. In order to standardize any language, stress must be laid upon the widest possible use of that language. The more a language is used, the more it attains a living condition. A language is used across diverse spheres such as education, communication, literature, administration, law and industry. For this purpose, periodicals must be published together with the compilation of dictionaries and grammars. Where the linguistic differences are distinct, the language itself is distinct; otherwise it is a regional variety of the same language, but in Nepal's context the eastern variety is likewise a dialect, yet it has attained the position of the standard. And yet the Nepali language had its origin in the Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces themselves. Matters stand such that the speech spoken in the very place of the language's origin is a dialect, whereas the Nepali spoken in the far east is a language. The chief reason why the Nepali spoken in the Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces is not standard is precisely the want of use; the substance drawn out in this article is that, if stress is laid upon its use in the very course of using the Nepali language, the speech of this region can be standardized.
australian_english: This study homes in on working out a work direction for standardizing the Nepali spoken in Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces. The article has been put together with the objective of building a work direction that standardizes the differences in the Nepali of Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces and locks in linguistic unity, and it works around the question of just how the standardization of the Nepali language of these provinces might be possible. The dialect groups spoken in these provinces were split into three main dialect groups — the western dialect group, the central dialect group and the Bheri regional dialect group — and, taking the author's own earlier study of them, done by studying them under that split, and the earlier studies done with this region as the base, the job of suggesting ways to standardize them has been done. The principle of standardization, which sits inside language planning under applied linguistics, has been made the theoretical groundwork for this article. To standardize any language, the weight has to go on people using that language a lot. The more a language gets used, the more it gets to a living state. A language gets used across all sorts of areas — education, communication, literature, administration, law, industry and the rest. For that, dictionaries and grammars need to be built and periodicals published alongside. If the linguistic differences are distinct enough, the language itself is a different language; if not, it is a regional variety of the same language — but in Nepal's case the eastern one is a dialect too, yet it has picked up the status of the standard. Yet the Nepali language itself started out right in Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces. So you get the language spoken right where it was born called a dialect, while the Nepali spoken away in the far east is called a language. The big reason the Nepali of Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces isn't standard is simply that it isn't used; the gist drawn out in this article is that if the push goes on its use in the very course of using the Nepali language, the language of this region can be standardized.
informal_english: This study is all about putting together a game plan for standardizing the Nepali spoken in Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces. The article's aim is to lay out a game plan that standardizes the differences in the Karnali and Sudurpaschim Nepali and keeps the language united, and it's built around the question of how standardizing the Nepali of these provinces could even work. The dialect groups spoken in these provinces got split into three main ones — the western group, the central group and the Bheri regional group — and then, going off the author's earlier study of them, done by studying them that way, and the earlier studies done in this area, the job of suggesting how to standardize them got done. The principle of standardization, which sits under language planning in applied linguistics, is the theoretical base here. To standardize a language you've really got to push people to use it a lot, eh. The more a language gets used, the more alive it stays. A language gets used in all kinds of places — education, media, literature, government, law, industry, you name it. For that you need dictionaries and grammars, plus papers and magazines coming out alongside. If the differences are big enough, it's a whole different language; if not, it's just a regional version of the same one, but in Nepal the eastern one is a dialect too, yet it's the one that ended up as the standard. And yet Nepali actually started right there in Karnali and Sudurpaschim. So the language spoken right where Nepali was born gets called a dialect, while the Nepali way out east gets called a language. The main reason the Nepali in Karnali and Sudurpaschim isn't standard is just that people don't use it enough; the gist here is that if you keep pushing its use while Nepali is being used, this region's language can be standardized for sure.
translator_notes: कार्यदिशा rendered throughout as 'work direction' (no settled English equivalent); ढाँचाको लेख treated as the article's framing question. Sentence order follows the source exactly.
